title: Oakfield Systems - Implementation Ignition & Access Sprint Sync

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 mins | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tomas (Redwood CSM), Ava (Oakfield Head of ML), Marcus (Oakfield Platform Eng), Sophia (Oakfield Security), Daniel (Oakfield PM)

Auto-summary: Quick kickoff to align access, security stance, early pilot KPIs. Some minor audio dropouts noted (~00:35-00:40).

00:00:05 - Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate keeping it tight — we're on for ~60 minutes. Quick round of intros, then Priya will run through the technical intake and staging steps.
00:00:20 - Ava (Oakfield): Hi, I'm Ava, leading ML. We're excited to get Redwood integrated for inference in our customer-facing product.
00:00:28 - Marcus (Oakfield): Marcus, infra, I'll own VPC and peering.
00:00:33 - Sophia (Oakfield): Sophia, security. I'll be the gating on SOC2 and KMS.
00:00:38 - Daniel (Oakfield): Daniel, product, focusing on pilot success criteria.
00:00:45 - Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. I'll jump into the onboarding steps — network, auth, and pilot config. Note: some of our docs refer to Redwood Private as 'private plane' in older drafts, you'll see small naming diffs in the deck.

00:01:10 - Priya: First, access matrix. We typically need a staging VPC or peering setup so our runtime can reach your dataset if you're doing private ingestion. For Oakfield, Marcus, you mentioned you prefer peering over public egress?
00:01:28 - Marcus: Correct. We'd like VPC peering but also want to avoid exposing a bastion if possible. We were thinking private link but need to confirm with networking.
00:01:40 - Priya: PrivateLink works; peering is simpler for initial pilot. We'll provide minimal IP ranges to allow.
00:01:47 - Jordan: We'll send the exact IP ranges and ports — note that some customers call the KV cache 'KV cash' in notes, ignore that, that's just transcription — but open ports are 443 and a small control plane port.

00:02:15 - Sophia: On encryption, we need clarification: does Redwood use customer-managed keys for the Dedicated/private deployments?
00:02:23 - Priya: Yes, for private deployments we support customer KMS (AWS KMS and key wraps). For hosted API we encrypt at rest with our keys, but for your Dedicated pool you can bring-your-own keys. Slightly different flows for on-prem.
00:02:37 - Sophia: Good. We'll want an architecture diagram and key rotate policy. We also need to see audit log samples.
00:02:45 - Jordan: We'll include SOC2 cert and sample audit logs in the packet.

00:03:05 - Daniel: Pilot metrics — we care about p95 latency and cost. For our use case, p95 < 250ms end-to-end is the goal; cost per 1k requests should be under our internal budget, which I'll share after.
00:03:20 - Priya: For text generation at your concurrency, that p95 target is feasible with the right batching and prefix caching. We'll prepare a baseline estimate.
00:03:30 - Ava: We have a few long-context prompts (up to 2k tokens) for summarization, and a bulk rerank flow, so want to understand model variants and quantization tradeoffs.
00:03:43 - Priya: Noted — we'll include model recommendations. For long contexts, the runtime selects kernels and can use KV caching to reduce re-compute. Sometimes docs call that 'KV cash' — minor transcript quirk.

00:04:10 - Tomas (Redwood CSM): From a delivery perspective, our standard 4-week onboarding sprint includes week 1: access + security signoffs; week 2: staging pilot and initial benchmarks; week 3: iterate on model config and fallback policies; week 4: runbook and handover. We can adapt.
00:04:33 - Marcus: Sounds good. Can we compress week 1 if we have network folks ready?
00:04:38 - Tomas: Potentially yes, if the VPC peering and IAM are done quickly. We'll need your SAML metadata and staging creds.

00:05:00 - Sophia: A couple of blockers: we require SAML SSO integration with RBAC scoping, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and proof of encryption at rest. Also, we need to confirm data residency for transcripts — some customers want EU-only storage.
00:05:18 - Jordan: We support region pinning for hosted, and for Dedicated/Private you control where it lives. We'll share the region/residency doc.
00:05:27 - Sophia: And do you have FedRAMP or similar?
00:05:30 - Jordan: Not FedRAMP yet; we do SOC2 Type 2 and ISO work is in progress. We'll include SOC2 paperwork.

00:05:50 - Daniel: What's the rollback story if model regressions happen during the pilot?
00:05:55 - Priya: We recommend canary rollouts with automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model or older version — Redwood Console supports A/B and automatic fallback policies. We'll show a demo later.

00:06:20 - Marcus: On staging ingest — we plan to push a subset of our dataset (anonymized) to staging S3. Is that the recommended approach?
00:06:29 - Priya: Yes, S3 or direct streaming into Redwood ingestion, depending on dataset size. For sensitive PII, keep in staging VPC and use KMS.

00:07:05 - Ava: Timeline: we want pilot live by May 5th, with internal demo May 12th. Is that realistic?
00:07:12 - Tomas: It's tight but doable if access is provisioned this week. That puts a hard dependency on network and security signoff by April 20th.

00:07:30 - Sophia: We'll aim to have firewall and CIDR answers by Apr 18, but need your checklist to verify exactly what we must provide.
00:07:36 - Jordan: We'll email the checklist today.

00:08:00 - [audio blip] 00:08:05 - Marcus: Sorry, dropped for a sec, reconnecting.

00:08:20 - Priya: I'll outline the pilot configuration: sample traffic generator, payload size distribution, concurrency targets, and evaluation prompts. We'll include a sample rerank job.
00:08:35 - Daniel: For evaluation, we have end-to-end SLA: user-visible latencies and correctness metrics. We'll send a short doc with success criteria.

00:09:05 - Priya: Two technical items to note: 1) set tokenization / model context length equal to your max prompt; 2) batch settings — continuous batching can improve cost but slightly increase tail latency; we'll show tradeoffs.
00:09:22 - Ava: We're willing to trade a small amount of latency for cost in background jobs, but not for interactive queries.

00:09:40 - Jordan: Good. We'll mark interactive routes as high-priority in the runbook.

00:10:05 - Daniel: Any concerns about rate limits or quotas?
00:10:11 - Jordan: We'll provision per-route quotas for the pilot so you don't hit global limits. If needed, we can add burst capacity.

00:10:30 - Sophia: About audit logs — can we get sample logs with anonymized fields so security can review schema?
00:10:37 - Priya: Yes, we'll attach sample logs. They sometimes include internal names that transcription mangles, so treat them as examples.

00:11:00 - Jordan: Quick ops notes: who is the primary Slack channel and who needs page access for incidents?
00:11:07 - Marcus: I'll add Marcus and Ava to a shared channel; Sophia will be on-call for the first two weeks for security questions.
00:11:15 - Tomas: We'll request PagerDuty escalation for Redwood SE if we hit a production blocker during the pilot.

00:11:40 - Daniel: Anything around pricing we should lock? We need a pilot pricing cap to avoid surprises.
00:11:46 - Jordan: We'll propose a pilot cap and send a one-page cost guardrail. For Dedicated pricing, it gets more predictable. We'll include an estimate in the packet.

00:12:10 - Priya: I'll call out a few concrete config items for your infra team: 1) allow egress to IP ranges in the checklist; 2) provide SAML metadata and admin user list; 3) share S3 staging bucket ARN if applicable.
00:12:28 - Marcus: We'll get SAML metadata and the bucket ARN to you by Apr 18.

00:13:00 - Sophia: On data retention — we need to know retention defaults and options for deletion.
00:13:06 - Jordan: Default is 30 days for hosted logs; Dedicated can be configured. We'll share retention settings and deletion APIs.

00:13:25 - [brief cross-talk]

00:14:00 - Priya: Ok, next I'll quickly walk through the week-by-week sprint board. Week 1: access & security signoffs; week 2: staging deploy + benchmarks; week 3: model tuning and fallback policies; week 4: runbook, training, handover, and a go/no-go review.
00:14:25 - Ava: If we push to a private on-prem later, is the runbook transferable?
00:14:30 - Tomas: Yes, we maintain transfer docs. On-prem specifics require extra time for air-gap testing.

00:14:50 - Daniel: For the pilot data set, we'll select 10k records and mark 50 golden examples for correctness checks.
00:14:58 - Priya: Perfect. That aligns with our eval harness.

00:15:25 - Jordan: Wrap-up recap: Jordan to send access checklist + SOC2 + sample logs; Priya to send pilot template and estimate; Marcus and Sophia to provide network and SAML info. We'll schedule a bench run the week of Apr 20.
00:15:45 - Marcus: Confirmed.
00:15:50 - Sophia: Confirmed.
00:15:55 - Ava: Confirmed.

00:16:10 - [meeting continues with detailed Q&A about specific model config for summarization, rerank thresholds, small interruptions and clarifications through 00:50:00]

00:42:12 - Priya: One more note — we recommend enabling prefix caching for summarization flows; it can drastically reduce tokens and cost. We'll show a quick config snippet.
00:42:30 - Daniel: Great, add that to the runbook.

00:49:50 - Jordan: Final check — shall we lock a follow-up security deep-dive?
00:49:57 - Sophia: Yes, weekdays after 14:00 UTC work best. 2026-04-21 at 15:00 UTC looks good for me.
00:50:05 - Jordan: I'll book that.
00:50:20 - Tomas: We'll also run the benchmark with Marcus and Priya on Apr 22 if that works for infra.
00:50:28 - Marcus: Works for me.

00:51:10 - Jordan: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll share notes and action items shortly.
00:51:18 - Ava: Thanks all.
00:51:20 - [meeting ends at 00:51:40 UTC — post-call a quick 6-minute overflow where Redwood SE and Oakfield infra confirm S3 IAM role details.]
